newsitem.title: CHINA: China executes crime spree cop and 23 others.
newsitem.headline: China executes crime spree cop and 23 others.

text.p: Chinese authorities have executed 24 criminals, including one policeman who promised to protect his partners in crime from the law, state media said.
Authorities in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen sentenced 15 criminals to death at a public sentencing rally last week, the Shenzhen Economic Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Friday.
All 15 were executed shortly after being sentenced, the newspaper said.
Executioners in northwestern Shaanxi province last weekend shot a gang of eight thieves and a policeman who had promised to protect them from the law, the Shaanxi Daily said.
Policeman Liu Qingkui had sold stolen goods for his partners in crime during a five-year spree and had assured them their security was guaranteed, the newspaper said.
Liu and the eight others were shot immediately after a public sentencing rally, it said.
Chinese officials say frequent use of the death penalty is essential to combat a rising tide of crime around the country.
Human rights watchdog Amnesty International recorded 2,535 executions in China in 1995 compared with 1,791 in 1994. Many executions are believed to go unreported.
